title: punchlist worker report
description: What a worker hands back after one attempt at one step. Adapters translate each runtime's native output into this shape. A report is evidence for the runner and the planner; it never decides pass or fail, and its cost fields never default to zero.

status.description: done: the worker believes it finished (acceptance will tell). partial: it stopped before finishing but left a usable checkpoint; `checkpoint` is required and the runner may start a continuation attempt. blocked: it needs something it cannot get; `questions` is required. failed: it gave up or was stopped by a limit with nothing to hand on.

stop_reason.description: Why the worker process ended, as observed by the adapter, independent of what the worker claims.

summary.description: What was done, in the worker's words, within the step's max_summary_chars. Not an assessment of correctness.

checkpoint.description: Handoff for a continuation attempt, which starts with a fresh context, the step packet, this checkpoint and the current diff. The alternative to compacting a long-running worker's context in place.

changed_files.description: Computed by the adapter from git, never from the model: run `git add -A -N` first so untracked files appear, then `git diff --numstat -M -z` for counts and renames and `git diff --raw` for symlinks and mode changes. Plain `git diff --numstat` misses untracked new files.

evidence.description: Raw material the planner can look at without re-reading the repo. Bounded on purpose.

questions.description: Required when status is blocked. Each should be answerable in one line; a human answer written in progress.md unblocks the step on resume.

basis.description: reported: the runtime stated the cost. configured_price: computed from tokens and the lane's configured prices. known_zero: the lane is declared free (local model, script). unknown: none of the above; the budget gate never treats this as zero.

quota_fraction.description: For subscription-backed lanes: the share of the window this attempt consumed, as observed by the configured quota source (difference of two observations).

source.description: Which source produced the number, e.g. claude-code-usage, api-headers, price-table.
